rows: Let me show you a grip instead of describing one. Watch my hands, not my mouth.
I can brawl when it is needed. Most of the time it is not needed.
Risk is a grip that slips. I would rather you took the slow route with me.
Stalling is just waiting with better manners. I prefer to be doing something.
The people want to see control, and control looks quiet until it is finished.
Short version: the hold tells the story, and I am not in a hurry to finish it.
I am known for doing the sensible thing very well. That is my reputation.
Look at the stance. It is patient, not passive.
You say technique. Show me the grip you trust, and I will show you mine.
Strikes are loud. Control is quiet and wins more often.
A risk is only useful if you can hold it when it goes wrong. Can you?
Slow is not weak. It is the choice that stops you moving.
The people deserve work they can follow. Give them a grip they can see.
You talk of being among the best. Let us see you hold something.
You are proud of your {strength}. Good. Pride is useful when it is quiet.
I have watched your {strength} closely. It is clearer than you think.
You kept calm. Good. Calm is the right place to start a hold.
Fair. We will both know soon enough.
I could tell you what I think of that. I would rather show you on the mat.
One fall. Keep me down and I will admit the hold was clever.
On the mat I will go slowly, and you will feel every step.
Grounded or standing, the grip decides it, not the noise.
Stay where you are. I want to see if you can hold your position.
Good answer. Now let us see it on the mat.
You have not answered. I will wait.
Fair. That is a grip I can work with.
I accept that. We can settle it on the mat.
I will hold this match with patience, and I will not let go early.
I am going to wrestle carefully and finish with control.
Whatever happens, you will know exactly where you were when it finished.
It is not finished yet. I am still counting holds.
I have one more hold in mind. You will feel it when it arrives.
